bullets: Sunspots: cooler dark magnetic patches; 11-year cycle - matched by plasma currents in the 35,000-km-deep Near-Surface Shear Layer (LENS, May 2025).

Flares/CMEs hit satellites, GPS, aviation, radio, power grids; cause auroras . Aditya-L1 showed the Oct 2024 storm strongly compressed Earth's magnetic shield (TH, 11 Jan 2026). ESA-China SMILE (Vega-C) will image the solar wind-magnetosphere link (LENS, Apr 2026).
Sunspots: cooler, darker regions of intense magnetic activity; markers of the ~11-year solar cycle (minimum to maximum); the Sun's magnetic poles reverse at each peak (LENS Feb 2026).
Solar flares: sudden bursts of radiation from magnetic reconnection, classed A, B, C, M, X (X strongest). CMEs: plasma clouds from the corona at 250-3,000 km/s, reaching Earth in 1-3 days.
Effects on Earth: geomagnetic storms, auroras, damage to satellites, communication, navigation and power grids.

bullets: The increasing-wavelength order of electromagnetic radiation is gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, microwaves, and radio waves.

Radio waves are used for radar detection and ranging.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-1 › Earthquakes - causes, seismic waves, measurement, distribution, effects › Volcanic products and types
bullets: Products: pyroclastic debris, ash, volcanic bombs, lava. Gases: mostly water vapour, then CO2, SO2, H2S .
Strombolian eruptions are frequent, mild bursts of bombs and ash. Vulcanian eruptions are more explosive (LENSD, 19 May 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-1 › Volcanoes - types, materials, landforms, global distribution › Magma vs lava, chamber, vent, crater, caldera; monitoring instruments
bullets: Magma = molten rock below the surface (in a magma chamber); lava = magma that reaches the surface through the vent.
Crater = funnel-shaped mouth at the top ; caldera = cauldron-shaped depression formed when the magma chamber empties after a big eruption and the summit collapses.
Tiltmeter measures ground tilt over faults and volcanoes; creepmeter measures fault slip (APPSC 2018; anemometer measures wind speed, not direction).
